gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed supratentorial glioblastoma isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type classification (2021 World Health Organization Classification of Tumours, 5th Edition, Volume 6)

candidate_evidence.quote: This is a randomized, open-label, phase 2 study evaluating the safety and efficacy of oral ropidoxuridine as a radiation-sensitizing agent

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Ropidoxuridine as a Radiosensitizer in Newly Diagnosed IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma With Unmethylated MGMT Promoter

tumour_pk_planned_evidence.quote: Maximum plasma concentration for orally administered ropidoxuridine, at dose levels of 960 and 1200 mg once daily.

role_evidence.quote: Ropidoxuridine is administered daily, 5 days a week, for 7 weeks, starting one week prior to radiotherapy, and then concurrently with a standard 60 Gy radiotherapy, followed by a 4-week rest period.

agents.drug_class_hint: investigational oral halogenated pyrimidine nucleoside radiosensitizer (5-iodo-2-pyrimidinone-2'-deoxyribose)

source_quote.quote: with unmethylated O6-methylguanine-DNA-methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter (defined as MGMT methylation status ≤20% by pyrosequencing

coder_notes: Two randomised experimental dose arms (960 vs 1200 mg) plus an efficacy cohort compared to historical controls; no control arm. PK is plasma only. Temozolomide is only an optional post-study maintenance at investigator discretion, not a protocol agent, so not listed. Ropidoxuridine is not described as a prodrug in the record; formulation_flag none.
